questions.text:
Let G = (V, E) be any connected undirected edge-weighted graph. The weights of the edges in E are positive and distinct. Consider the following statements:

(I) Minimum spanning tree of G is always unique.
(II) Shortest path between any two vertices of G is always unique.

Which of the above statements is/are necessarily true?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- (I): distinct weights [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] unique MST True
- (II): two different paths can have equal total weight even with distinct edges (e.g. 1 + 4 = 2 + 3) False

Answer: (I) only

questions.text:
A multithreaded program P executes with x number of threads and uses y number of locks for
ensuring mutual exclusion while operating on shared memory locations. All locks in the
program are non-reentrant, i.e., if a thread holds a lock l, then it cannot re-acquire lock l
without releasing it. If a thread is unable to acquire a lock, it blocks until the lock becomes
available. The minimum value of x and the minimum value of y together for which execution
of P can result in a deadlock are:
questions.solution:
The locks are non-reentrant: if a single thread holding lock l tries to acquire l again, it blocks forever waiting for itself. So one thread and one lock are enough.

Answer: x = 1, y = 1

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

At x = 1: numerator 1 [latex]-[/latex] 2 + 1 = 0, denominator 1 [latex]-[/latex] 3 + 2 = 0. L'Hospital:
[latex]\frac{7x^6-10x^4}{3x^2-6x}\Big|_{x=1}=\frac{-3}{-3}=1[/latex]

Answer: is 1

questions.text:
Let p, q, and r be propositions and the expression (p[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]q)[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]r be a contradiction. Then, the
expression (r[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]p)[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]q is
questions.solution:
[latex](p\rightarrow q)\rightarrow r[/latex] is always false, so [latex]p\rightarrow q[/latex] is always true and r is always false.

Then [latex]r\rightarrow p[/latex] is true (r is false), so [latex](r\rightarrow p)\rightarrow q\equiv q[/latex]. It is true exactly when q is true.

Answer: always TRUE when q is TRUE

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: always TRUE when p is FALSE
always TRUE when q is TRUE

questions.text: Let u and v be two vectors in [latex]R^{2}[/latex] whose Euclidean norms satisfy ||u||=2|| v|| . What is the value of [latex]\alpha[/latex] such that w=u+[latex]\alpha[/latex]v bisects the angle between u and v ?
questions.solution:
The bisector points along the sum of the unit vectors: [latex]\frac{u}{\|u\|}+\frac{v}{\|v\|}=\frac{u}{2\|v\|}+\frac{v}{\|v\|}=\frac{1}{2\|v\|}(u+2v)[/latex].

So w = u + 2v bisects the angle: [latex]\alpha=2[/latex].

Answer: 2
